headline: Tresoldi hattrick helps Brugge stun Inter Milan 4-3 in Champions League thriller
summary: Club Brugge delivered a shocking 4-3 defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League, with Nicolo Tresoldi scoring a hat-trick. The Italian champions remain on zero points after two matches.
details: Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolo Tresoldi shocked Inter Milan 4-3 in the Champions League on Tuesday. The 22-year-old Italian-German forward scored the first three goals for the Belgian side.

Tresoldi converted a penalty just before the half-hour mark after a Hakan Calhanoglu foul. He then capitalized on a goalkeeping blunder by the Inter keeper for his second goal and reacted faster than the Inter defense for his third, completing a hat-trick with a quarter of an hour to go.

Lautaro Martinez had given Inter a lifeline just before the break and narrowed the score to 3-2 in the 81st minute. However, Romeo Vernant once again exposed Inter's defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal for Brugge in the 87th minute.

Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side after 93 minutes, but it was not enough. The reigning Italian champions and Serie A leaders remain stuck on zero points after losing to Real Madrid and Brugge.
Inter Milan will be under immense pressure to win next week at home against Shakhtar Donetsk. Club Brugge, who were defeated at home by Aston Villa on matchday one, will next host French club Lens.
caption:
Nicolo Tresoldi scored a hat-trick as Club Brugge delivered a stunning 4-3 defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League.

Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolo Tresoldi shocked Inter Milan 4-3 in the Champions League on Tuesday. The 22-year-old Italian-German forward scored the first three goals for the Belgian side.

Tresoldi converted a penalty just before the half-hour mark after a Hakan Calhanoglu foul. He then capitalized on a goalkeeping blunder by the Inter keeper for his second goal and reacted faster than the Inter defense for his third, completing a hat-trick with a quarter of an hour to go.

Lautaro Martinez had given Inter a lifeline just before the break and narrowed the score to 3-2 in the 81st minute. However, Romeo Vernant once again exposed Inter's defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal for Brugge in the 87th minute.

Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side after 93 minutes, but it was not enough. The reigning Italian champions and Serie A leaders remain stuck on zero points after losing to Real Madrid and Brugge.

Inter Milan will be under immense pressure to win next week at home against Shakhtar Donetsk. Club Brugge, who were defeated at home by Aston Villa on matchday one, will next host French club Lens.

headline: Saudi Arabia strikes Yemen's capital Sanaa as Houthis threaten oil sites amid escalating war
summary: Saudi-led coalition forces have targeted Yemen's capital Sanaa, prompting Houthi rebels to warn of a 'harsh and painful' response against major Saudi oil facilities, intensifying the conflict.
details: Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Yemen's capital Sanaa on Tuesday, according to Houthi media. This comes as the Iran-aligned Houthi group threatened retaliation against Saudi oil facilities, marking a rapid escalation of the ongoing war.

Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that a Saudi-led coalition hit the Yemen Petroleum Company’s Sabah central station, a fuel depot on the outskirts of Sanaa. The coalition had previously advised civilians to evacuate the site.

Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree warned of a 'harsh and painful' response to any strikes, naming Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran and an oil refinery in Riyadh as potential targets. The group also reiterated warnings for oil workers in Saudi Arabia to avoid sites that might be attacked.

Saudi Arabia's cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, stated that the Houthis would face consequences for their repeated attacks on the kingdom. This escalation follows a Houthi ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport that reportedly killed 13 people.

Yemen’s civil war reignited last month after Houthis advanced along the Red Sea coast towards the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. This strait is crucial for global energy shipments, especially since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia has sought international support, with Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan assuring Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of Ankara's solidarity. US President Donald Trump also spoke with the Saudi Crown Prince, stating that the Houthis were 'behaving very badly'.

Despite Washington's reluctance to be drawn directly into the conflict, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi offered on Sunday to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, a proposal reiterated by Tehran's foreign ministry.
